rationale: Internally consistent and mechanically coherent (sequencing establishes purpose, mix establishes provenance), but it is a moderator-for-moderator swap between the archive's two highest-t counterparty signals, so it carries real risk of fitting the same underlying Δ-operating-liability effect a third time rather than adding new information.

This is a statistical blend of two archive legs motivated explicitly by diversification of t-stats rather than by a single economic mechanism — payout composition and trade-credit expansion have no common causal story, and averaging a leg with a null slope into one with a null alpha is a cosmetic recombination, not a new hypothesis.

Substituting net external financing for gross issuance in an existing archive expression is a measurement tweak of Counterparty_Versus_Market_Funding_Mix, and the resulting leg is close to the well-documented net-external-financing anomaly interacted with R&D intensity, a configuration the archive has already tested several times.

Moving the gate from 0.03 to 0.10 is threshold tuning on an already-tested expression, and because the indicator discards the continuous intensity weighting that produced the positive result, any sign change will be confounded with a large coverage/composition shift rather than cleanly resolving the population question it claims to settle.

The zero-inflation objection is legitimate, but because issuance is non-negative the leg's sign is determined entirely by −Δ(operating liabilities), making this an issuance-magnitude reweighting of the archive's already-established positive counterparty leg with the sign flipped — the "substitution" mechanism therefore cannot be separately identified from the base effect.

Applying the ratification structure to purchased rather than organic intangibles targets a largely disjoint population where accounting value is least verifiable and impairment lags longest, which is a genuine extension; the main hazard to diagnose is that consolidating an acquiree mechanically inflates operating liabilities, so serial acquirers may be misread as counterparty-validated.
